envelope.name: Whisper
envelope.request: Add a whisper(text) function in src/whisper.js that returns the text in lower case with three dots at the end. Export it from src/index.js with tests.

spec.summary: word-tools is a small library of text helpers that programmers can use in their own code. This change adds a new helper called whisper. It takes a piece of text, makes the first letter a capital and everything else lower case, and adds "..." on the end, so "hELLO WORLD" becomes "Hello world...".

features.title: Add whisper(text) and export it from the package entry point
features.story: As a developer using word-tools, I want a whisper(text) helper that I can import from the package entry point. It should return my text with only the first letter capitalised, everything else in lower case, and three dots on the end.
acceptance: Importing whisper from src/index.js gives a function
whisper("Hello World") returns "Hello world..." (only the first letter of the whole text is capitalised, not the first letter of every word)
whisper("Wait...") returns "Wait......" (dots are always added, even if the text already ends with dots)
whisper(" hi") returns " hi..." (only the very first character is upper-cased, so a leading space stays a space)
whisper(42) throws a TypeError with message "whisper expects a string"
The existing capitalize tests still pass, and capitalize is still exported from src/index.js
src/whisper.test.js exists and npm test exits with code 0

assumptions: whisper follows the same pattern as capitalize: an ES module named export in its own file, src/whisper.js, re-exported from src/index.js, with a one-line doc comment.

Following the owner's change: only the very first character of the whole text is upper-cased. Everything after it is lower-cased, including the first letters of later words. "Hello World" becomes "Hello world...".

The capitalising rule is the same as the existing capitalize helper: upper-case text[0] and lower-case the rest. If the text starts with a space or punctuation, that character is left as is, so whisper(" hi") returns " hi...". It does not skip ahead to the first letter.
Non-string input throws a TypeError with the message "whisper expects a string". whisper checks this itself, so the message names whisper and not capitalize.
Three dots are always added, even if the text already ends with dots or other punctuation. whisper("Wait...") returns "Wait......".
The dots are three ASCII period characters ("..."), not the single ellipsis character (…).
Case changes use JavaScript's standard toUpperCase()/toLowerCase(), with no locale-specific rules.
The README gets a short whisper(text) section next to the capitalize one, so the new helper is documented.
Tests use the built-in node:test and node:assert/strict, like the existing tests, so no dependencies are added.
spec.uiContract:
- This is a library, so it has no UI, routes or HTTP endpoints. The contract is the module API.
- Existing (do not change):
- src/capitalize.js exports capitalize(word). It upper-cases word[0], lower-cases the rest, returns "" for "", and throws TypeError("capitalize expects a string") for non-strings.
- src/index.js contains export capitalize from "./capitalize.js";.
- src/capitalize.test.js stays unchanged and must keep passing.
- package.json is an ES module ("type": "module"). The test script is node --test.
- New:
- File src/whisper.js has a named export export function whisper(text).
- If typeof text !== "string": throw new TypeError("whisper expects a string"). This check must come before any call to capitalize so the message is whisper's own.
- If text === "": return "...".
- Otherwise return text[0].toUpperCase() + text.slice(1).toLowerCase() + "...". Importing and reusing capitalize from "./capitalize.js" after the type check is fine, because it gives the same result.
- src/index.js adds the line export whisper from "./whisper.js"; and keeps the capitalize export.
- Test file src/whisper.test.js imports test from "node:test", assert from "node:assert/strict", and whisper from "./index.js" (the entry point, not ./whisper.js).
- Example values: whisper("hELLO") === "Hello..."; whisper("Hello World") === "Hello world..."; whisper("hELLO wORLD") === "Hello world..."; whisper("SHH") === "Shh..."; whisper("already quiet") === "Already quiet..."; whisper("") === "..."; whisper("Wait...") === "Wait......"
- README.md gets a section ## whisper(text) placed before ## Tests, stating that whisper("hELLO wORLD") returns "Hello world...".
